_: THE case table. ADR-035 §2.10: 'one data file, read by both the pgTAP suite and
Vitest, asserting equality to the centavo. Not two copies of the same expectations.'
The expectations here were NOT derived from this package. They were worked out by
hand in supabase/pgtap/07_money_and_units.sql (plan task 3.5) BEFORE any TypeScript
existed, and lifted across by `id` — that ordering is deliberate and is recorded in
docs/PLAN.md step 3: writing this file first would let it be shaped to whatever an
implementation already does, which is the drift it exists to prevent.
⚠️ EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS A DECIMAL STRING, NOT A JSON NUMBER. A JSON number
is an IEEE754 double in JavaScript, and 0.073 is not 0.073 in one. §2.5 rule 1 says
no floating point anywhere in the money path; a bare `0.073` here would put one in
the money path at the moment the file is parsed, before any code runs. Both readers
take these as text and scale them to integers themselves.
⚠️ THE HALF-CENTAVO BOUNDARIES ALL SIT IN `round(unit_price × qty)`, NEVER IN THE
TAX STEP. §2.5 asked for 'a half-centavo boundary per tax rate', which reads as
though the tax division has one. It does not and cannot — proved by exhaustion in
07 F9 and F18, and §2.5 now carries the correction. A boundary case placed in the
tax split discriminates nothing and looks correct.

scales._: Decimal places each field carries, matching the applied schema: numeric(12,2) money, numeric(14,6) per-base price, numeric(14,3) base quantity, numeric(5,4) rate.

_: WHICH CASES CARRY WHICH RULE, NAMED so that deleting one turns a guard red
rather than letting the table quietly lose its teeth. Every id here is
asserted to exist, and to still have the property it is named for, by BOTH
readers — `07` F19-F21 and the Vitest suite's first block.
⚠️ ALL THREE GROUPS LIVE IN `round(unit_price × qty)`, AND THAT IS A RESULT,
not a coincidence. Neither tax step can produce a half-centavo tie at the two
rates this schema carries (07 F9 and F18, by exhaustion), and both of the
failures below happen only AT a tie — so the multiplication is the only place
either can be caught. §2.5 already says this of the rounding direction; plan
task 3.6b measured that it is equally true of the float.
_away_from_zero: The only cases that can tell §2.5 rule 6 (half-up AWAY FROM ZERO) from
JavaScript's Math.round (half-up toward +∞). The two agree on every positive
number, so the sign is the only place they differ — a discriminating case must
be a NEGATIVE line whose unit_price × qty lands on a half centavo. M8 is the
sell side, B6 the buy side. 07 falsifications S6, S14, S23 and S24.
_float_representation: The only case that can tell exact integer arithmetic from IEEE754. Added in
3.6b on the owner's decision (2026-09-01), because the table could not fail
for a float before it: the four boundaries it already carried — 0.365, 6.465
and their reversals — are ties a double happens to hold EXACTLY.
⚠️ IT DISCRIMINATES ON THE TYPESCRIPT SIDE ONLY. Postgres computes the anchor
in `numeric`, so 07 answers 3.48 whatever happens and this case is an ordinary
boundary there. It is in the shared file because it is the only thing standing
between packages/money and a float rewrite.
_residual_tax: The cases where §2.5 rule 4's residual and the spelling it forbids —
round(net × rate) — give different answers. Rule 4 has teeth only on the SELL
side, where the net is reached by division; on the buy side the two are
provably the same number for every net and rate (§2.5 rule 4's own warning,
asserted in 07 F17), so no buy case here is possible.
⚠️ THE TWO ERR IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and that is why there are two. M9's
forbidden spelling is a centavo LOW (1.65 against a residual of 1.66); M11's
is a centavo HIGH (0.35 against 0.34). A broken split that is off by a
consistent sign would pass a table of same-direction cases. M9 carried this
rule alone until 3.6b — found by falsification V3 in task 3.6a, where
breaking rule 4 turned exactly two tests red and both were M9's.
